prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1189; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment grew to many times the usual amount for this injury, with near-daily visits and new body areas added weeks after the crash.
- Records show long-standing treatment for the same condition before the crash; most of the current complaints come from it.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: The claimant reported a side impact at an intersection and a wrist fracture from the collision. The injury description fits the kind of force a side impact of this type would produce.

Entry 2: The police report places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene, and the responding officer's notes are consistent with the account given at first contact.

Entry 3: Two independent witnesses and the other driver each described the collision the same way the claimant did. Scene photographs were also received and reviewed.

Entry 4: The damage to the claimant's vehicle lines up with the described impact point and direction. No earlier damage to the vehicle has come to light in our review.

Entry 5: The claimant has given the same account in each conversation so far, with no changes in sequence or detail. The driver is named on the policy, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 6: Medical records show the claimant was receiving treatment for the same wrist and arm condition well before this collision. Most of the current complaints appear to trace back to that earlier condition.

Entry 7: Treatment has grown to many times the usual course for this type of fracture, with near-daily visits. Several weeks after the collision, new body areas were added to the claim without a clear link to the crash mechanics.

Entry 8: The file has been referred for a medical review of the pre-existing records and the treatment timeline. Settlement discussions are on hold until that review is complete.
